title: Sushan's reply to Herman
summary: Sushan answers that Brown's willingness must be sought first and circulates the letter to the board.

blocks.x: Now read Sushant. I'm reading it. I don't want to know them.

This is a letter headed. New Orleans Jazz Club, 2417 Octavia Street, New Orleans 15, Louisiana. October 18, 1957. Mr. David L. Herman, 107 Camp Street, New Orleans 12, Louisiana. Dear Dave Cullen, I read with interest your letter of October 14th relative to your client, Mr. Nicola Riker, and the possibility of an appearance by him and by Mr. Tom P. Brown to present proof and facts supporting their respective claims. Period. New paragraph. Before any plans could be made for such an occasion, comma, it is necessary that we have some expression for Mr. Brown that he would be willing to participate, period. I am sending him a copy of this letter, comma, with a request that he advise me his disposition in the matter, period. New paragraph. In the meantime, comma, I am sending copies of your letter to all members of the board of directors of the New Orleans Jazz Club as a matter of interest and for their information, period. I personally feel that could be gained from the standpoint of the history of jazz if such discussions are conducted, period. New paragraph. With best wishes, comma, I am sincerely Harry V. Sushant, President and Son, Harry. Now, turn your back. Just a second. CC, Mr. Thomas B. Brown, 1228th Street, New Orleans, comma, Louisiana. All right. Would you like Mr. Brown's letter?
